mappedContracts.statement: Bind credentials and cookies to verified HTTPS origins, paths, and redirect destinations.
acceptanceCriteria: Cookie headers are computed per request from a scoped cookie jar.
Substack cookies are never forwarded to arbitrary publication or redirect hosts.
Redirects are handled manually and re-authorized.
Custom domains and canonical Substack API origins are modelled separately.

mappedContracts.statement: Distinguish authentication from authorization and require verified publication identity and role for every mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: Publication ID, role, origin, and current authority are checked immediately before mutation.

mappedContracts.statement: Enforce an explicit workspace boundary for every CLI and MCP filesystem read or write.
acceptanceCriteria: Resolve real paths and reject traversal, absolute-path escape, symlink/junction escape, UNC escape, and case-folding escape.
Only approved regular files under declared roots are accepted.
Media and fixture operations enforce size, type, and resource limits.

mappedContracts.statement: Redact and classify sensitive data structurally before any value reaches console, logs, MCP output, traces, fixtures, errors, or CI artefacts.
acceptanceCriteria: No raw arbitrary error string is persisted.
Correlation uses one-way fingerprints rather than partial secret disclosure.
Run-log privacy levels default to minimal.
Secret-scanner tests use synthetic credentials only.

mappedContracts.statement: Maintain an evidence-backed threat model for CLI, browser, internal API, official API, MCP stdio, MCP HTTP, registry distribution, state storage, and supply-chain boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Threats include credential exfiltration, SSRF, prompt/argument injection, path traversal, confused deputy, replay, duplicate mutation, supply-chain compromise, PII leakage, and malicious repository content.
Each threat maps to controls, tests, residual risk, and owner.
The model is reviewed for each release.
